voice.text: We pour the <emphasis>same juice</emphasis> into a tall cup, a round bowl, and a wide dish. [pause] Does the juice keep one shape of its own? Tap your guess.
Everything around you is stuff called <emphasis>matter</emphasis>. [pause] All matter has mass — you can weigh it — and it takes up space. [pause] Even air!
<emphasis>Solids keep their own shape.</emphasis> [pause] Put a block in a cup — it is still a block.
<emphasis>Liquids take the shape of their container.</emphasis> [pause] Pour the same juice into three cups: three shapes — but it is the same juice.
<emphasis>Gases spread out to fill all the space they can.</emphasis> [pause] Air fills the whole balloon. Air is not nothing — it is a gas, and it is matter too.

Heating and cooling change the form. [pause] Heat melts solid chocolate into liquid chocolate. More heat boils water into a gas called steam. Cold freezes water into ice. [pause] And listen: it is the <emphasis>same stuff</emphasis> every time. Melted chocolate is still chocolate!
